claims.claim: For a simple undirected graph, mean degree is 2m/n.
The density of a simple undirected graph is 2m/[n(n−1)].
Local clustering is the fraction of possible neighbor-neighbor edges that exist; NetworkX uses zero when degree is below two.
Average local clustering is the arithmetic mean of node coefficients; transitivity is a distinct triangle/triple ratio.
claims.locator: Average clustering definition; compare transitivity API

claims.claim: NetworkX average_shortest_path_length requires a connected undirected graph or strongly connected directed graph.
claims.locator: Raises section and disconnected graph notes

claims.claim: For edges (0,1),(1,2),(2,0),(2,3), density=2/3, mean local clustering=7/12, transitivity=3/5 and average path length=4/3.
claims.locator: Definitions applied to the explicit four-node graph in this lesson
